preamble: Backing of the labiodental fricative [f] to the velar fricative [x] occurs in three settings. In Old Dutch, [f] before [t] became [x] (craft > kracht, after > achter), a dissimilation shared with neighbouring Low German but not with German or English. In Southern Russian and Ukrainian, which historically lacked /f/, foreign [f] is replaced by [x] or by [xv]~[xw] (Church Slavonic Ѳома > Ukrainian Хома). In Andalusia and parts of Spanish America, /f/ before the labial glide /w/ is articulated as an aspirate or a velar fricative (fuerte, fuego, fuente).

examples.note: Regular change ft > xt; compare German Kraft, English craft.
The obsolete variant graft preserves the older form.
Southern Russian and Ukrainian dialects replace foreign /f/ with [x] or [xv]~[xw].
Before /w/, /f/ is articulated as an aspirate or a velar fricative in Andalusia and parts of Spanish America.
